newsitem.title: USA: Lockheed Martin wins bomb kit competition.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed Martin wins bomb kit competition.

text.p: The U.S. Air Force announced the selection of Lockheed Martin Corp to produce 40,000 "smart tail kits" for bombs in a $500 million program to sharply increase the accuracy of the weapons.

Lockheed Martin won out in a competition with Alliant Techsystems Inc to produce the kits. They will allow the bombs to use global positioning satellites to compensate for wind and other factors after they are dropped from high altitude by U.S. warplanes.

The Air Force said the first 40 kits will be delivered this spring and that the weapons would be initially assigned to B-52 bombers and F-16 attack jets and later to F-117A "stealth" fighters, F-15E attack jets and B-1 bombers.

Asst. Air Force Sec. Arthur Money called the "wind corrected munitions dispenser" program "extremely successful" and other service officials said it will result in high accuracy even if bombs are dropped from altitudes of 30,000 feet, out of the range of anti-aircraft weapons.

Lockheed Martin was awarded a $21 million contract to get the program going, but the Air Force said that follow-on production contracts for the tail kits are expected to increase the total program to about $500 million.
